{{Recipe summary | Category = Beverage recipes | Time = 10 minutes | Difficulty = 1 }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]] | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]] '''Lemonade''' is a sweetened [[Cookbook:Beverages|beverage]] made from lemons, sugar, and water. It is popular in the United States during the spring and summer, when it is generally served chilled with ice. In some countries, the word 'lemonade' is also used to describe any clear carbonated drink; in others, it means any fruit-flavored soda. == Ingredients == * 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]/8.5 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) fresh [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] juice * ¾–1 cup (160–225 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]/5.6–7.9 oz) [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white]] or [[Cookbook:Turbinado Sugar|turbinado]] sugar * 5–6 cups (1.2–1.5 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]]) [[Cookbook:Water|water]] == Special equipment == * Citrus [[Cookbook:Citrus reamer|reamer]] == Procedure == # Combine the lemon juice and sugar in a pitcher or jug. Stir until the sugar is dissolved. # Stir in the water. # Chill and/or serve over ice. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *Using turbinado sugar will result in a golden-brown color and mild caramel flavor. *Because sugar dissolves easier in warm liquid, you may want to heat some of the water and dissolve the sugar in it before combining with the remaining ingredients. *Hard lemonade incorporates an alcoholic spirit, such as [[Cookbook:Tequila|tequila]], [[Cookbook:Gin|gin]], or [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]] to the lemonade. *Various fruits, such as [[Cookbook:Strawberry|strawberries]] and [[Cookbook:Raspberry|raspberries]] can be added for color and flavor. A small amount of [[Cookbook:Beet|beet]] juice results in pink lemonade with little change in flavor. *[[Cookbook:Herb|Herb]]s such as [[Cookbook:Mint|mint]], borage, [[Cookbook:Lavender|lavender]], and [[Cookbook:Lemon Verbena|lemon verbena]] can change the aroma of the drink. *Including the lemon peels, bruised and sliced, gives more bite and a stronger aroma. *Other citrus fruits can be used, including [[Cookbook:Lime|lime]], [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]], and [[Cookbook:Grapefruit|grapefruit]]. Sugar and water content should be adjusted to taste. In American parlance, these are not technically lemonades, but limeade, orangeade, etc. *The sugar can be replaced by other alternative sweeteners. [[Category:Recipes for lemonade]] [[Category:Recipes using lemon juice]] [[simple:Cookbook:Lemonade]] [[Category:Recipes using white sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using turbinado sugar]]
